keywords.def: revision of what is already memorised
the checklist used to assess recitation

questions.q: Score this example against the rubric: a pupil recites Al-Fatihah fluently but says ٱلْحَمْدُ with a 'h' instead of ح.
questions.a: Hifdh 4; makharij 2 (ح said as ه); rules 4; fluency 4; target: ح from the middle of the throat.

questions.q: In the portal response box, write your hifdh target, one tajweed target and your weekly revision plan (sabaq, sabqi, manzil). Today's rota group recites Al-Fatihah and one short surah.
questions.a: A realistic plan: e.g. sabaq 'Abasa 1 to 8; sabqi last week's ayat; manzil 114 to 100 over the week.

questions.q: Extend: choose the time of day you will revise and why.
questions.a: For example: after Fajr, when the mind is fresh.

questions.q: Stretch: explain why revising old surahs matters as much as learning new ones.
questions.a: Memorised Qur'an escapes without revision (Bukhari and Muslim: it escapes faster than camels from their hobbles).

options: older surahs revised on a rota
questions.a: A) older surahs revised on a rota. Sabaq is new ayat; sabqi is recent; manzil is the older memorised portion revised on a rota.

questions.q: New ayat for today are called ...
Think again: A footballer practises the same basics every day. What are the 'basics' of good recitation, and why practise them again in Year 7?
questions.a: Correct makharij, sifat and rules: in Key Stage 3 we move from knowing rules to using them without thinking.
